svg.title: xor.ad panel — how a control behaves
svg.desc: Redrawn from panel/src/App.css. Three laws, the matrix of variants against states, what the keyboard does. Hover changes the fill and nothing else; the shadow is the height, and only a press spends it.

g.text: Redrawn from App.css. Hover firms the fill; the depth never changes; a press travels its own distance and lands on its shadow.
the gap never changes; the fill firms up. Only :active travels its 4
2 · FOCUS IS THE FRAME, ONE LINE
no ring, no outline. 3.07:1 against the resting frame — over the 3:1 needed
3 · WHAT PERSISTS FILLS, AND KEEPS ITS PLACE
one baseline. No shadow, because it is in the row rather than on it
Three variants exist in the CSS — the plain one, .button-primary and .button-danger. Nothing else does.
never held — a primary does a
thing, it is not a mode
accent wins — focus is not intent
Intent sets the fill and the ink. Geometry — frame, height, shadow, travel — is the same for all three, so a mixed row still sits on one line.
Disabled overrides intent entirely: the fill goes back to --surface, the frame to --line, the label to --ink-muted. Nothing fades.
hover moved −2, then grew the gap 4 → 6 — the row breathed either way
hover changes the fill only — the gap never changes
focus on the inverted button was accent on ink — 2.82:1
transform and box-shadow eased 90ms; fill and frame snapped
nothing eases — the whole state arrives at once
disabled was opacity .5 — it faded the label with everything else
frame --line, label --ink-muted, fill --surface. Fields and ticks too
:active outranked aria-pressed, so a held button left the row when clicked
:not([aria-pressed="true"]) on :active — what is held stays held
one button; the variants lived only in the mockup
.button-primary and .button-danger, on five and two places
A checkbox is a control, so it behaves like one.
It used to travel −1 −1 under the pointer, and then it grew its gap instead — in a column of fifteen scopes, fifteen things moving because a
pointer crossed them. It now does what a button does: the fill firms up and nothing else changes, and a click spends its own 2px of depth.
panel/design/button-states.svg — redrawn from the stylesheet after 1b · 2a · 3b · 4a · 5b · 6c. The matrix is what the code does today.
Every state on this sheet is a record of what the stylesheet does, not a proposal.
